reasoning: The claim is entirely accurate. In March 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo played a historic five-game match against Lee Sedol, a 9-dan professional who held 18 international titles and was widely considered the world's top Go player of the era. AlphaGo won the match 4 games to 1. Prior to AlphaGo's breakthrough, AI experts and Go professionals widely believed that a computer program defeating a top human professional was at least a decade away, making the 2016 victory "a decade ahead of schedule" in the eyes of the scientific community.
